# pr-2301: fix(2276): job-stop KILL round keeps the pre-reap root set; survivors adopted

## Description

## Mechanism fixes (issue #2276)

- **KILL round re-root (AC2):** `LocalShell.killTree` (non-ownGroup walk path) no longer re-roots walk #2 at the possibly-reaped leader pid (which made `ps` return `{}` and SIGKILL nothing). It re-roots at the TERM round's own victim set: every walk-#1 pid still observable (reaching fully-orphaned survivors whose rows are reparented to init) plus their live descendants (forks during the grace). The recycled-pid trade is the same accepted scan-then-signal race as before, now noted at the walk.
- **Truthful survivor adoption (card b):** the #2201 survivor scan now runs on stop exits (job stop/timeout/cancel and exec timeout/cancel) gated by `shouldScanSurvivors(stopped, ownGroup)` — scans only where the tree kill was a best-effort walk (non-ownGroup, e.g. macOS without setsid); ownGroup hosts keep the gh-1053 group-kill contract byte-identical (AC3, pinned by a REG test). The registry settle listener already adopts whatever `SurvivorReporting` buffers, so survivors of a stopped job get re-tracked instead of the tool answering "Stopped" while a TERM-trapping grandchild lives on.
- **Doc truth:** the false "gh-1053 reaped those trees" premise is corrected in `SurvivorReporting`, `ShellExecResult.survivors`, the `_listenSettle` adoption comment, and the `stopSurvivors` getter doc.

Fixes #2276

## Tests

New seam-driven suite `test/env/io_execution_env_kill_tree_test.dart` (no real processes): red-first pinned the bug — with the old re-root, walk #2 receives `{100}` and the KILL round never fires; now walk #2 receives the full pre-reap victim set and the TERM-trapping grandchild reaches SIGKILL. REG: ownGroup stop never walks or walk-signals; vanished-tree walk #1 sends nothing; `shouldScanSurvivors` truth table (stop × ownGroup).

Local gate: `dart analyze` clean on all touched files, `dart format` exact, new suite + `shell_jobs_test` (40) + `adopted_shell_jobs_test` (37 pass / 3 ps-leg skips) green.

# Review Policy

Preset: `default` — resolved from: built-in default (resolution chain: projectConfig.reviewPolicy → workflow jobParams → built-in default).
Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.
Every verdict on this PR is traceable to this table.

| Severity | Round | Fix | Gates approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🚨 BLOCKING | rework | mandatory | YES |
| ⚠️ IMPORTANT | rework | mandatory | YES |
| 💡 SUGGESTION | polish | mandatory | no |
| 🪶 NIT | none | opportunistic | no |

Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.

Bounds: polishMaxThreads=6 · polishMaxChangedLines=80 · opportunisticMaxThreads=8 · opportunisticSameFilesOnly=true · densityMin=2 · densityMax=8 · sweepBatch=10 · sweepMaxAgeDays=30

Density cap (💡/🪶 threads only; 🚨/⚠️ never capped): allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8).
Rank your findings and post the top-K as threads; the overflow becomes a ranked digest list in the general comment. The census counts posted threads + digest lines.

Machine enforcement: the approval is recomputed from the severity census + this policy — the model verdict is advisory. Any 🚨 or ⚠️ open → REQUEST_CHANGES; only 💡/🪶 → APPROVE.
## Downgrade protocol

A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification** in the census (the thread reply and the response summary: why this is not maintainability debt). A silent downgrade does not exist: the next review round re-raises it as ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. A justified downgrade lets a false-⚠️ review converge to APPROVE without a code change.

# pr-2301: fix(2276): job-stop KILL round keeps the pre-reap root set; survivors adopted

## Description

## Mechanism fixes (issue #2276)

- **KILL round re-root (AC2):** `LocalShell.killTree` (non-ownGroup walk path) no longer re-roots walk #2 at the possibly-reaped leader pid (which made `ps` return `{}` and SIGKILL nothing). It re-roots at the TERM round's own victim set: every walk-#1 pid still observable (reaching fully-orphaned survivors whose rows are reparented to init) plus their live descendants (forks during the grace). The recycled-pid trade is the same accepted scan-then-signal race as before, now noted at the walk.
- **Truthful survivor adoption (card b):** the #2201 survivor scan now runs on stop exits (job stop/timeout/cancel and exec timeout/cancel) gated by `shouldScanSurvivors(stopped, ownGroup)` — scans only where the tree kill was a best-effort walk (non-ownGroup, e.g. macOS without setsid); ownGroup hosts keep the gh-1053 group-kill contract byte-identical (AC3, pinned by a REG test). The registry settle listener already adopts whatever `SurvivorReporting` buffers, so survivors of a stopped job get re-tracked instead of the tool answering "Stopped" while a TERM-trapping grandchild lives on.
- **Doc truth:** the false "gh-1053 reaped those trees" premise is corrected in `SurvivorReporting`, `ShellExecResult.survivors`, the `_listenSettle` adoption comment, and the `stopSurvivors` getter doc.

Fixes #2276

## Tests

New seam-driven suite `test/env/io_execution_env_kill_tree_test.dart` (no real processes): red-first pinned the bug — with the old re-root, walk #2 receives `{100}` and the KILL round never fires; now walk #2 receives the full pre-reap victim set and the TERM-trapping grandchild reaches SIGKILL. REG: ownGroup stop never walks or walk-signals; vanished-tree walk #1 sends nothing; `shouldScanSurvivors` truth table (stop × ownGroup).

Local gate: `dart analyze` clean on all touched files, `dart format` exact, new suite + `shell_jobs_test` (40) + `adopted_shell_jobs_test` (37 pass / 3 ps-leg skips) green.

**Disclosure:** this dev Mac cannot run the real-process ps legs (`/bin/ps: Operation not permitted` in the sandbox), so verification here is unit/seam only — the existing real-process legs (`io_execution_env_test`, `shell_job_io_test`, `agent_cli_waiting_integration_test` — incl. the walk-fallback AC3 leg) execute on CI-Linux.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.
- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.
- `lib/src/a2a/` — Agent2Agent client/server/manager (`fa serve --a2a`).
- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles → `docs/cubes.md`; `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` — HEP event protocol → `docs/hep.md`.
- `lib/src/web_search/` — `web_search` (DDG keyless → keyed providers); `tool/fa-clip/` — native macOS pasteboard helper.

**packages/ + app shells:**

- `packages/fa_ui/` — reusable widgets (incl. trajectory) → `docs/agents/fa-ui.md`; `dap_hub`, `fa_llm`, `fa_llm_mock` → `docs/dap.md`.
- `flutter_app/` — the Flutter app (desktop/mobile/web) → `docs/agents/flutter-app.md`; services one-liner: `docs/agents/services.md`; JS apps: `docs/agents/js-apps.md`; HomeKit/Calendar/CodeMie: `docs/agents/system-integrations.md`.
- `browser_ext/` + `lib/src/browser/` + `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — browser extension + WebSocket bridge → `docs/browser-extension.md`.
- `office_addin/` + FA_HOST=office app host — Office add-in → `docs/outlook-addin.md`.
- `fa_network` — external Go backend bridged via the DAP hub (channel-id caveats: `docs/dap.md` §14).
- `site/`, `scripts/`, `docs/subagents/` — landing page (privacy sync), gates + codegen, subagents master plan → `docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md`.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(`.fah/memory/note/` since gh-2185 — local-only, not committed; the
user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/goldens/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/goldens` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

## Prompts live outside Dart code

Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;
flutter_app/packages → +flutter; scripts/.github → everything. Invariants:

- analyze + format clean; `dart test` green — **deterministic-only**
  (mock LLM; live models never in the gate; `llm`-tagged files run only in
  the tag-only provider smoke + nightly).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80%; jscpd < 1% core / < 3.7% app; cross-module
  dup < 0.31%; CRAP ratchet: core 12.0, app 30.0 (thresholds only-down);
  ≤ 2800 lines per `.dart` file; AGENTS.md ceiling (top of this file).
- Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json`; nightly keeps running quarantined files.

Full gate text: `docs/agents/quality-gates.md`; CI workflows: `docs/ci.md`.

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type exists on BOTH the CLI
and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in
`cliOnlySettings`/`appOnlySettings` (`lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`)
with the reason; run `dart test test/parity/`. Host capabilities (issue
#1079): every host-wiring capability declares its 7-host matrix state AT
BIRTH (`on` / `off(reason)` / `transport`) via `wireAgentCore` — `off` is
invisible everywhere; extensions are declared surface, SDK invariants have
no override point. Full rules: `docs/agents/cross-platform-parity.md`.

## Commits and releases

- Commit as `ai.teammate <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (set repo-locally);
  subjects `type(scope): ...`. Release-path automation MUST use the
  fa-release-bot GitHub App token — never a PAT or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Every push to main cuts an annotated tag (`scripts/auto_release.sh`);
  the tag is the single version source (pubspecs stay `0.0.0-dev`);
  releases go DRAFT-first and publish at `release-provenance` only with
  signed SHA256SUMS attached. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only (`## Unreleased`).
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag (first publish of a new
  package is manual); every lockfile is committed and enforced
  (`scripts/check_lockfiles.sh`); TestFlight external-group + store
  pipelines have required repo variables.

Full text: `docs/agents/commits-releases.md`.

## Bench

Bench knobs (agent timeouts, stall/watch, `FA_CONN_DEBUG`, hang replay,
report semantics) → `docs/bench.md` (round-3 knobs: issue #1392).

## Docs index

`docs/README.md` indexes every canonical doc (agents/, memory-churn,
compaction, dap, cubes, redaction, hep, ci, bench, browser-extension,
outlook-addin, …). New docs must be listed there.

## Mechanism (verified)

- `io_execution_env.dart:515-525` — walk#1 TERM(all) → grace → `victims = await _descendantsOf(pid);` re-roots at the leader: if the leader exited and the VM reaped it, `ps` no longer lists it → `:542` returns `{}` → KILL round hits nothing. TERM-ignoring grandchildren were reparented to launchd and are invisible to a root-at-pid walk.
- `shell_jobs.dart:553-556` — stopped/timed-out jobs report NO survivors, comment: "[[BUG] Foreground bash timeout kills only the direct child — a surviving grandchild holds the output pipe and the tool call never returns (run 36421037356 hung 10 min on flutter test) #1053](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1053) reaped those trees" — false exactly on non-ownGroup hosts where the walk misses reparented children; [[GOAL] Adopt detached background processes: foreground-bash survivors (& / nohup bypass) detected at exit → adopted into the job registry (waiting row + bash_job), completion auto-notified to the agent, boot re-adopts previous-run 'lost' jobs — no background process stays invisible #2201](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/2201)'s adoption would otherwise re-track the leftovers.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (integration, non-setsid host):** background job `sh -c 'trap "" TERM; sleep 300 & wait'`; `bash_job stop` → after ~1s no live process matches the job's command — today the trapping grandchild survives while the tool answers "Stopped".
- **AC2:** walk#2 re-roots at the SURVIVORS of walk#1 (children whose parent died), not at the possibly-reaped leader.

## Border cases

- Leader alive but ignoring TERM: today's KILL round catches it (walk#2 sees it) — unchanged.
- Racing forks during grace: the re-rooted walk widens correctly.

SPAWNER=$!

echo "spawner=$SPAWNER sh=$SHPID sleep=$SLEEPID"
ps -o pid=,ppid=,stat=,command= -p $SHPID 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/sh-row: /'
ps -o pid=,ppid=,stat=,command= -p $SLEEPID 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/sleep-row: /'
# check sleep's inherited TERM disposition
if [ -n "$SLEEPID" ]; then grep SigIgn /proc/$SLEEPID/status | sed 's/^/sleep SigIgn: /'; fi

import subprocess, sys, collections

roots = [shpid] if int(shpid) in parent else []

res = set(live); q = list(live)
while q:

#!/bin/bash
# Discriminating shape: grandchild traps TERM (via subshell trap + exec), leader does NOT.
sh -c '(trap "" TERM; exec sleep 606.3391) & wait' &
SH=$!
sleep 0.3
SL=$(pgrep -P $SH 2>/dev/null | head -1)
echo "sh=$SH sleep=$SL"
grep SigIgn /proc/$SL/status 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/sleep SigIgn: /'
grep SigIgn /proc/$SH/status 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/sh SigIgn: /'
echo "--- walk#1: TERM both ---"
kill -TERM $SH $SL 2>/dev/null
sleep 0.6
echo "after TERM round:"
ps -o pid=,stat=,comm= -p $SH 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/sh-row: /' || echo "  sh GONE+reaped"
ps -o pid=,stat=,comm= -p $SL 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/sleep-row: /' || true
python3 - "$SH" "$SL" <<'PY'
import subprocess, sys, collections
shpid, sleepid = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
out = subprocess.run(['ps','-ax','-o','pid=,ppid='],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
parent = {}
for line in out.splitlines():
    cols = line.strip().split()
    if len(cols) >= 2:
        try: parent[int(cols[0])] = int(cols[1])
        except ValueError: pass
def walk(roots):
    live = {r for r in roots if r in parent}
    children = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for pid, ppid in parent.items(): children[ppid].append(pid)
    res = set(live); q = list(live)
    while q:
        p = q.pop()
        for c in children.get(p, []):
            if c not in res: res.add(c); q.append(c)
    return sorted(res)
print("OLD walk#2 (root {sh}):", walk({shpid}) or "{} — EMPTY (old bug: KILL round no-ops, grandchild survives)")
print("NEW walk#2 (root {sh,sleep}):", walk({shpid, sleepid}) or "{}")
PY
kill -KILL $SL 2>/dev/null
echo "cleanup: sleep killed"
EOF

Verified empirically on Linux this round (real `ps`, real processes): in the leg's shape `trap "" TERM; sleep 606.2276 & wait`, the trap is set **before** the background fork, so TERM is `SIG_IGN` in **both** the job shell and the sleep (`/proc/<pid>/status` → `SigIgn 0x5006` on both — bit 15 = SIGTERM). The leader therefore survives the TERM round, is still observable in `ps` at walk #2, and **both** the old re-root (walk #2 at the bare leader pid) and the new re-root (walk #2 at the pre-reap victim set) return the same KILL set `{sh, sleep}` — the grandchild dies either way, so this leg cannot red-fail a future regression of the re-root this PR exists for. Only the seam test (`walks[1] == {100, 200, 300}`) pins that semantics.

This also tempers the merged-thread claim that the leg exercises "leader reap/reparenting and pre-reap KILL re-root" — in this shape the leader is never reaped, so neither the reap timing nor the reparented-row observability filter (`_descendantsOf`'s `roots.where(parentOf.containsKey)`) runs over a **real** table in the bug's configuration.

Ask (optional polish, one line + same teardown): make the shape discriminating, e.g.

```dart
final entry = await registry.start('(trap "" TERM; exec $marker) & wait');
```

The subshell traps TERM before `exec`, so the sleep keeps `SIG_IGN` while the outer job shell takes the **default** TERM → it dies and is reaped mid-grace; only the pre-reap re-root then reaches the reparented grandchild. Replayed over a real Linux table: old walk #2 = `{}` (grandchild survives → this leg would go red) vs new walk #2 = `[<survivor>]` (leg green). Everything else (marker polling, `pkill` teardown, 30s timeout) stays as-is.

## PR #2301 re-review (round 2) — fix(2276): job-stop KILL round keeps the pre-reap root set — **APPROVE**

**Review artifacts written** (posting-review session, no pool-specialist prompt in `input/`):
- `outputs/pr_review.json` — APPROVE, census `{blocking:0, important:0, suggestions:1, nits:0, digest:1}`, `findingReview` dispositions
- `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-paragraph general comment (Summary / Key Issues / Next Steps)
- `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md` — one 💡 SUGGESTION thread @ `test/env/io_execution_env_kill_tree_test.dart:213`

### Registry dispositions (both prior ⚠️ verified fixed)
- **F1 (call-site survivor-adoption untested) → fixed.** Hunks cited: `io_execution_env.dart:886,897` (timeout/aborted `ExecutionError.survivors`), `:1043-1054` + `:1345-1353` (both scan call sites gated by `shouldScanSurvivors`), `builtin_tools_bash.dart:560-563` (Err-path adoption before retry/throw). Tests delivered exactly as asked: stopped non-ownGroup registry job adoption (`kill_tree_test.dart:127-196`), timeout'd exec carrying survivors on its error (`:171`), plus tool-level Err adoption (`adopted_shell_jobs_test.dart:211-251`).
- **F2 (AC1 real-process leg missing) → fixed.** `kill_tree_test.dart:196-246`: `ownProcessGroupOverride = false`, `trap "" TERM; sleep 606.2276 & wait` behind `entry.stop()`, polls the real `ps` table for marker absence; ps-gated, CI-runnable.

### Fresh verification this run (Linux, `ps` available)
`dart analyze` clean on all 5 touched files (+ shell_jobs.dart) · kill-tree suite **8/8 including the real AC1 leg** (skipped on the author's Mac — ran here) · `adopted_shell_jobs` + `shell_jobs` **81/81** · `dart format` exact.

### New finding (1 × 💡 SUGGESTION, with fresh empirical evidence)
The AC1 leg **passes identically under the old buggy re-root**: I replayed both kill rounds over a real Linux table — the leg's command traps TERM *before* the background fork, so the ignore is inherited (`SigIgn 0x5006`, bit 15, on **both** sh and sleep); the leader is never reaped, and old walk#2 (root at bare pid) returns the same `{sh, sleep}` as the new pre-reap re-root. The leg pins the walk machinery but not the fix — only the seam test pins the re-root. One-line polish offered and validated: `(trap "" TERM; exec $marker) & wait` (leader takes default TERM → dies/reaped → old walk#2 = `{}` → leg red; new = `[survivor]` → green). Digest line: exec-path scan can race the in-flight KILL round (`io_execution_env.dart:996`) and adopt a process the round reaps ~400 ms later — benign, liveness-only, auto-pruned.

No CI failures file present; nothing blocking. Per the verdict table (only 💡 remains, both ⚠️ resolved with citable hunks) the machine verdict converges to APPROVE.
